name: Scope Creep Is a Timing Problem
title: Scope Creep Is a Timing Problem, Not a Willpower Problem
subtitle: The same change costs a sentence in a requirements meeting and a sprint once code exists to contradict it.

cover.alt: Scope creep is a timing problem, not a willpower problem: a region filter is an easy change early, expensive rework mid-sprint, the sprint is already full, a silent yes hides the cost, a visible tradeoff is reprioritization. What comes out to make room?
cover.caption: Same request. Different cost.
cover.use: Cover: top of the post (and Substack social preview)

substack.email_subject: "Can we also filter by region?" costs nothing. Until it doesn't.
substack.note:
"Can we also filter by region?"

In a requirements workshop, that's one sentence added to a document nobody has built against yet.

Three days into the sprint, the same sentence means unwinding a data model, a query and two components.

The request didn't get bigger. The number of things it contradicts did.
